cells: Force of water compresses air in cracks causing rocks to break.
Rock fragments carried by waves grind coastal rocks.

blocks.content: Hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, and solution are the primary mechanisms through which ocean waves continuously erode coastal landforms.

rows: Trapped air in rock fissures expands and contracts violently under wave pressure
Widens cracks and breaks off structural rock fragments
Waves hurl sand, gravel, and stones against the cliff base
Creates wave-cut notches and continuously undercuts cliffs
Swirling water causes wave-borne rocks to collide with each other
Rounds and shrinks rock fragments into smooth shingle and sand
Saline water and weak organic acids dissolve minerals within coastal rocks
Erodes soluble rock formations like chalk and limestone

items: Sequence of landform evolution (Sea Cave → Sea Arch → Stack → Stump) is a high-frequency topic in physical geography papers.
Differentiate Corrasion (mechanical grinding of rock by sediment) from Corrosion (chemical dissolution of rock minerals in seawater).
Wave-cut platforms mark the retreat of coastal cliffs over time and typically form at the high-tide level.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Marine erosion is driven by wave action, tides, currents, and storm surges impacting coastal zones.
The four main erosion processes are hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition, and solution (corrosion).
Hydraulic action compresses air in cliff crevices, causing explosive pressure that shatters rock faces.
Abrasion acts as a sandpaper effect, where waves hurl rocks and sediments against cliff bases.
Attrition reduces rock debris into smaller, rounded pebbles through continuous inter-particle collisions.
Erosional coastal features evolve in sequence: Sea Cave → Sea Arch → Stack → Stump.
